plan: Ten new items across all four domains with balanced choice lengths and near-miss distractors: colon-defined vocabulary, main purpose, cross-text sample critique, sensitivity-as-range data item, archaeological inference, complex-series semicolons, long-subject agreement, a reinforcing transition that resists a later contrast, two-part synthesis goal, central idea.

passages.title: Committee report
passages.text: Although the committee's final report ran to more than two hundred pages, its recommendations were notably ______: each could be carried out within a single budget year by the city's existing staff.

passages.title: Crater streaks
passages.text: For years, dark streaks that appear on the walls of certain Martian craters were widely thought to be traces of flowing salty water. When planetary scientist Teodor Lind compared the streaks' locations with maps of slope, however, he found that they occur only on slopes steep enough for dry sand and dust to slide on their own. Lind argues that the streaks are better explained as small avalanches of dry material.

passages.title: Four-day week (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Economist Rosa Iglesias argues that a four-day workweek raises productivity. She points to a group of firms where output per hour rose after employees switched to working four days a week.

Text 2
Labor researchers note that the firms volunteering for four-day-week trials tend to be ones whose managers already expect the change to succeed and whose work can easily be compressed into fewer days. Results from such firms, the researchers caution, may not hold for workplaces in general.

passages.title: Seed germination
passages.text:
A researcher measured the percentage of seeds that germinated for two wildflower species at three soil temperatures.
Soil temperature | Species X | Species Y
10°C | 12% | 40%
18°C | 55% | 62%
26°C | 81% | 58%
The researcher claims that Species X's germination is more sensitive to soil temperature than Species Y's is.

passages.title: Herd remains
passages.text: Archaeologists studying a 4,000-year-old village found that the sheep and goat bones in its earliest layers come almost entirely from young males; the females, by contrast, were usually kept into old age. Herders who raise animals mainly for meat tend to slaughter them young, whatever their sex, whereas herders who keep animals for milk tend to keep females into adulthood and cull most young males. The pattern in the village therefore suggests that ______

passages.title: Festival lineup
passages.text: This year's festival lineup includes the Ramos Quartet, a string ensemble from Lisbon ______ Aiko Tanaka, a percussionist from Osaka; and the Northfield Choir, which will close the final evening.

passages.title: Delta maps
passages.text: The hand-drawn maps that cartographer Ama Boateng produced during her survey of the river delta, many of which record channels that have since filled with silt, ______ now used by hydrologists modeling future floods.

passages.title: Early reception
passages.text: When it was first published, the novel was dismissed by most critics as a minor work. ______ its first printing of two thousand copies took nearly a decade to sell out. Only after the author's death did readers begin to treat it as a classic.

passages.title: Packaging notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mycelium is the root-like network of a fungus.
• Some companies grow mycelium around agricultural waste in molds to make packaging.
• Mycelium packaging is lightweight and absorbs shocks well.
• Unlike foam packaging, mycelium packaging breaks down in soil within a few weeks.
• Mycelium packaging currently costs more to produce than foam packaging does.

passages.title: Covered market
passages.text: Many visitors to the old covered market in Varos assume that its maze of alleys grew without any plan. Historian Selin Aydın's study of property records complicates that view. The market's oldest section, she found, was laid out on a deliberate grid around two stone storehouses; only the later additions, built as trade expanded, wandered outward along whatever streets already existed.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: each could be carried out within a single budget year by the city's existing staff
candidates.explanation: The colon explains the blank: recommendations that need no new staff and only one budget year are limited in scale, or "modest." "Although" contrasts that small scale with the report's great length.

A.rationale: "Sweeping" means broad and far-reaching, the opposite of what the colon describes.

B.rationale: "Concise" seems to contrast with the long report, but the colon describes how easy the recommendations are to carry out, not how briefly they are worded.

C.rationale: "Tentative" means uncertain; nothing suggests the committee was unsure.

hints: What does the clause after the colon say about the recommendations?
Does it describe their wording or their scale?

strategy.explanation: Predict "small in scale" from the colon clause, then match.

candidates.remember: The clause after a colon defines the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that the surface of Mars has never held liquid water of any kind
choices.B: To present a finding that supports a different explanation for a feature
choices.C: To describe the methods scientists use to map the slopes of Martian craters
choices.D: To explain why dry sand slides more easily than wet sand on steep slopes

candidates.evidence: Lind argues that the streaks are better explained as small avalanches of dry material
candidates.explanation: The text sets up the long-held water explanation, reports Lind's slope finding, and gives his alternative explanation, dry avalanches.

A.rationale: Lind challenges one explanation of the streaks; the text makes no claim about all water on Mars ever.

C.rationale: The slope maps are mentioned only as the source of Lind's evidence.

D.rationale: The text never compares dry and wet sand.

hints: What explanation does the text start with?
What does Lind do with that explanation?

strategy.explanation: Summarize: old view, new evidence, new explanation.

candidates.remember: Main purpose covers the whole text, not one detail.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the labor researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to Iglesias's claim in Text 1?

choices.A: By noting that the firms she studied may not represent workplaces in general
choices.B: By arguing that output per hour actually fell at the firms she studied
choices.C: By agreeing that every firm should adopt a four-day workweek at once
choices.D: By insisting that managers' expectations have no effect on trial results

candidates.evidence: Results from such firms, the researchers caution, may not hold for workplaces in general
candidates.explanation: Text 2 does not dispute the data; it questions whether volunteer firms are typical. So the researchers would say Iglesias's firms may not represent workplaces in general.

B.rationale: Text 2 never disputes that output rose at those firms.

C.rationale: Text 2 warns against generalizing, so it would not urge every firm to switch.

D.rationale: Text 2 suggests managers' expectations may matter, the opposite of this choice.

hints: Does Text 2 question the data or how far it applies?
Which choice matches that concern?

strategy.explanation: Find Text 2's caution and match it.

candidates.remember: Doubting a sample is different from doubting its data.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researcher's claim?

choices.A: At 26°C, Species X germinated at a rate of 81%, well above Species Y's rate of 58%.
choices.B: At 18°C, both species germinated at rates above 50%, with Species Y slightly higher.
choices.C: Across the three temperatures, Species X ranged from 12% to 81%, but Species Y only from 40% to 62%.
choices.D: Species Y germinated at its highest rate at 18°C rather than at the warmest temperature.

candidates.evidence: Species X's germination is more sensitive to soil temperature than Species Y's is
candidates.explanation: Sensitivity means how much germination changes as temperature changes. Species X changes by 69 percentage points; Species Y by only 22. Only C compares the ranges.

A.rationale: A higher rate at one temperature does not show how much the rate changes with temperature.

B.rationale: A single temperature says nothing about sensitivity to change.

D.rationale: Where Species Y peaks does not compare how much each species varies.

hints: What does "sensitive to temperature" mean in terms of the data?
Which choice compares change across temperatures for both species?

strategy.explanation: Define the claim's key term, then find the matching comparison.

candidates.remember: Sensitivity is about change, not about the highest value.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the villagers raised sheep and goats only for their wool and hides.
choices.B: the villagers kept sheep and goats at least partly to obtain milk.
choices.C: the villagers did not eat the meat of sheep or goats at any time.
choices.D: the villagers kept more goats than sheep in the village's earliest years.

candidates.evidence: herders who keep animals for milk tend to keep females into adulthood and cull most young males
candidates.explanation: The village shows the milk pattern: young males culled, females kept into old age. So the villagers likely kept the animals at least partly for milk.

A.rationale: The text offers no wool or hide pattern, and "only" is unsupported.

C.rationale: The culled young males were likely eaten; the text gives no reason to rule out meat entirely.

D.rationale: The text never compares the numbers of goats and sheep.

hints: Which of the two herding patterns does the village match?
Does the answer need to rule out meat entirely?

strategy.explanation: Match the village's pattern to one of the two described.

candidates.remember: Prefer the cautious claim the evidence fully supports.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: a percussionist from Osaka; and the Northfield Choir
candidates.explanation: The list's items contain internal commas, so the items are separated by semicolons, as the semicolon after "Osaka" shows. The same mark is needed after "Lisbon."

B.rationale: A comma would blur where the first item ends, since commas already appear inside the items.

C.rationale: A colon would introduce Tanaka as an explanation of the quartet.

D.rationale: A dash is inconsistent with the semicolon that separates the next items.

hints: What separates the second and third items in the list?
Should the first and second items be separated the same way?

strategy.explanation: Match the punctuation used elsewhere in the same series.

candidates.remember: Use semicolons between list items that contain commas.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: The subject is "maps" (plural); everything up to the blank modifies it. The sentence needs a finite plural verb: "are."

A.rationale: "Is" agrees with a nearby singular noun such as "delta," not with the plural subject "maps."

B.rationale: "Being" is not a finite verb, so the sentence would have no main verb.

D.rationale: "To be" is not a finite verb, so the sentence would be a fragment.

hints: Strip out the modifying phrases: what is the subject?
Does the sentence have a main verb without the blank?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate non-finite forms, then check agreement.

candidates.remember: Find the subject before the long modifiers.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: dismissed by most critics as a minor work
candidates.explanation: Slow sales reinforce the poor reception described in the first sentence; "Indeed" adds a stronger supporting point.

A.rationale: "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but slow sales are consistent with the critics' dismissal.

B.rationale: "Instead" signals a replacement, but slow sales do not replace the dismissal.

C.rationale: "Even so" signals a result despite the preceding fact, but slow sales follow from it.

hints: Do slow sales agree with or contrast with the critics' view?
The contrast comes in the third sentence, not the second.

strategy.explanation: Decide whether the sentence continues or reverses the idea, then match.

candidates.remember: Don't import a contrast from a later sentence.

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize an environmental advantage of mycelium packaging over foam packaging. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Grown from the root-like network of a fungus, mycelium packaging is lightweight and absorbs shocks well.
choices.B: Unlike foam, packaging grown from mycelium, the root-like network of a fungus, breaks down in soil within weeks.
choices.C: Though it is grown from a fungus, mycelium packaging currently costs more to produce than foam packaging.
choices.D: Some companies now grow mycelium, the root-like network of a fungus, in molds to make packaging.

candidates.evidence: Unlike foam packaging, mycelium packaging breaks down in soil within a few weeks.
candidates.explanation: The goal has two parts: an environmental advantage and a comparison with foam. Only B gives both: unlike foam, it breaks down in soil within weeks.

A.rationale: Light weight and shock absorption are practical, not environmental, advantages, and there is no comparison with foam.

C.rationale: This compares with foam but gives a disadvantage, cost.

D.rationale: This describes how the packaging is made, with no advantage or comparison.

hints: List the goal's parts: environmental, advantage, compared with foam.
Which choice meets all three?

strategy.explanation: Turn the goal into a checklist before reading the choices.

candidates.remember: Every part of the stated goal must be met.

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The market grew entirely without a plan, just as most of its visitors have long assumed.
choices.B: The two stone storehouses were the most profitable buildings in the whole Varos market.
choices.C: Property records are the most reliable source available for studying any old market.
choices.D: The market's oldest section was planned, though its later additions grew less systematically.

candidates.evidence: The market's oldest section, she found, was laid out on a deliberate grid
candidates.explanation: Aydın's records show the core was planned on a grid, while later additions followed existing streets: a mixed picture that "complicates" the no-plan assumption.

A.rationale: This is the visitors' view that the study complicates.

B.rationale: The storehouses' profits are never mentioned.

C.rationale: The text uses property records but makes no claim that they are the best source for any market.

hints: What view does the study "complicate"?
What did the study find about old and new sections?

strategy.explanation: State the finding in your own words, then match.
